Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We have a promising POC that’s about to convert to a Dedicated capacity deal (expected close: end of Q2). Before the contract, procurement has asked for a recommended GPU SKU plan and a short rationale we can attach to the purchase request.

Short context: our product ingests customer forms and runs a 6k-context retrieval+RAG LLM (open-model) for summarization + a separate embedding pipeline for semantic search. Peak expected concurrency: ~140 concurrent user sessions, average RPS ~250, but bursty at end of business day. Latency targets: p95 < 800ms for the RAG flow, embeddings can be async but need high throughput.

Can you send a one-page recommendation (H100 vs A100 vs L4) with memory/perf/cost tradeoffs and a suggested node mix? I attached a small sample of their workload.

Best,

Folks — did a quick pass on the sample and here’s a pragmatic recommendation we can present to NeoForms. Summary first, details below.

Recommendation (short): Hybrid pool: 2x H100 (80GB) + 3x A100 (40GB) + 8x L4 (48GB equiv for inference) as a starting committed reservation. Rationale: H100s host the large 70B retrieval model and keep KV cache for long contexts; A100s act as midsize workhorses for medium-context/throughput; L4s handle embeddings and low-latency small model inferencing at lower cost.

Why H100: best throughput for long-context attention and larger model weights; larger HBW memory is useful for multiple pinned RAG sessions and multi-tenant caching. Use H100s as the primary slot for p95-sensitive RAG traffic.

Why A100: good balance if customer wants consistent 40GB per card. Useful for batched offline jobs and fallbacks when H100 capacity is saturated.

Why L4: ~3-4x cheaper per token for small models and embeddings. Great for their embedding pipeline and for burst capacity for low-context interactions. We can autoscale L4 pool aggressively.

Suggested commitment math (based on sample workload):
- Target baseline: sustain ~80 concurrent RAG sessions on H100s (each H100 supports ~40 sustained RAG sessions at target latency with prefix caching) => 2 H100 GPUs pinned.
- A100 pool: support another ~60 concurrent medium-context sessions + batched offline workloads => 3 A100 GPUs.
- L4 pool: embeddings throughput (batching) + 2x headroom for bursts => 8 L4 GPUs.

Approx capacity notes:
- Memory constraints: H100 (80GB) allows >6k context + model weights comfortably; A100 (40GB) will require quantization or smaller sequence lengths for 70B-class models. L4 is suited for 7B-13B and embed-only models.
- Cost tradeoff (ballpark): relative hourly cost H100:A100:L4 ~= 4.0:2.0:0.6 — reflect in procurement doc.

Attachments I’ll provide: cost delta matrix and a nominal throughput chart. Linking the sample.

Marcus

Adding ops considerations — this will be important for NeoForms’ procurement and on-prem style checklist.

Node sizing & infra notes:
- H100 nodes: recommend 1x H100 (80GB) per host initially (or 2x with MIG disabled) to avoid cross-tenant interference and NVLink usage for large KV caches.
- A100 nodes: 2x A100 (40GB) per host is fine for batch-throughput workloads.
- L4 nodes: focus on high-density for throughput; 4-8 L4 per host depending on PCIe config.

Autoscale & fallback policy:
- Reserve H100 capacity for p95 RAG SLOs and configure automatic fallback to A100 when >85% H100 utilization for short windows (with associated latency increase notice).
- L4 should be autoscaled aggressively; cost-effective to burst here.

Ops/observability: include per-route token cost, KV-cache hit rates, and RT metrics in the SLO dashboard. Add a smoke test that runs the 6k-context RAG query on canary H100 after every deploy.

Security/compliance: customer asked about data residency — ensure private deployment nodes are in their VPC (we provide VPC option).

Dev

Alex / Sofia — thanks for the details and the sample. Here’s our recommended plan you can include in the procurement packet. I’ve kept it short and copy-ready.

Recommendation (for procurement):
- Commit: 2x H100 (80GB) + 3x A100 (40GB) + 8x L4 (in their preferred density)
- Purpose: H100s for p95-sensitive 6k-context RAG (pin KV caches), A100s for medium-context and batched offline workloads, L4 for embeddings and cost-efficient burst throughput.
- Memory/perf notes: H100 is strongly preferred for >4k contexts and large models (70B); A100 offers a 40GB alternative but will require quantization for the same model at full context. L4 provides excellent unit economics for 7–13B models and embeddings.
- Autoscale policy: reserve H100 with 15–20% headroom, allow A100 fallback for short windows, and autoscale L4 aggressively for embeddings.
- Ops checklist: include SLO smoke test on H100 canary, token-level cost telemetry, KV cache hit-rate dashboards.

Next steps:
